text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are AI systems that generate text by predicting the next word based on patterns learned from massive amounts of data. They are trained on huge collections of books, websites, and articles, which helps them understand language and answer questions. Users can improve results through prompt engineering—writing clear, specific instructions to guide the model's output. LLMs can write, summarize, translate, and explain ideas quickly, making them useful tools for learning and work. However, they have limits: they sometimes produce incorrect information, cannot truly understand meaning, and may reflect biases found in their training data.
